target_customer: Field service businesses and enterprises with deskless technician teams, initially in India and later trades and facilities companies
problem: Legacy ERP is rigid and most productivity tools target desk workers, so field teams run on paper and spreadsheets.
business_model: B2B SaaS with a single flat price and unlimited users, plus hands on configuration and data migration
product_category: Field service management software (began as no code mobile apps for field teams)

founders.name: Swaroop Vijayakumar
previous_startups: Product development agency that built about 60 internal apps for 20 companies (per YC launch post)
founders.background_notes: Described on the YC page as a 2x entrepreneur.

founders.name: Balakrishna Balasubramanian
previous_startups: Product development agency with Vijayakumar (per YC launch post)
founders.background_notes: Various software development roles per the YC page; employers not named.

investors: Same round as reported by YourStory

competitors.name: Retool
competitors.what: Low code internal tool builder; Fieldproxy launched as 'Retool for field teams'

technical_complexity.rationale: No code form and workflow builders with an offline mobile app are standard engineering, with offline sync the main hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Per customer configuration and data migration create stickiness, but field service software is crowded and the no code wedge is copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; incumbents did not displace it but it remains small.

market_need_then: The launch post says the founders built about 60 internal apps for 20 companies across consumer goods, mining, telecom, pharma and energy, showing repeated demand for mobile field apps.

identity.voice_and_tone: plain, anti legacy ('ditch the dinosaurs' page)

brand_strength.rationale: No brand press found; directories confuse it with unrelated firms of similar names.

pivots.from: No code mobile app builder 'Retool for field teams'
pivots.to: AI native field service management software
pivots.why: Not stated; current site pitches AI configured FSM for trades

outcome_analysis: Fieldproxy raised small rounds in India and has narrowed from a no code builder to AI field service management with named customers like Qube Cinemas. Indian Startup Times reports FY25 revenue of about Rs 1.0 crore with a loss, so it is surviving at small scale rather than scaling fast. Not a clear success or failure yet.
notes: Seed reported as Rs 2 crore (about $273K per a search snippet) by Entrackr and YourStory; amount left null as no conversion was checked on the page. Unverified single snippets: Rs 25 lakh from 100X.VC in 2021-03; a pre Series A of INR 6 crore reported by thestorywatch.com and dated 2022-07 or 2022-12 by CB Insights (conflict). Total raised estimates: $1.03M (Inc42) to $1.48M (CB Insights). Founding year given as 2016 and 2020; YC says 2020. Only one competitor is named by the company itself.
